title: Fewer subprocesses per factory-pipeline.py verb, pipeline lows, the workspace reader guard in scoped QA, path and model-hash gaps

tasks.grade_reason: the pipeline every plugin plan runs; a stale cache could report a wrong task state or a wrong agent
tasks.objective: Backlog topics test-speed-followups and run-lows-followups (docs/plans/backlog.md). Measured on main 8a2843e on Windows: `factory-pipeline.py status docs/plans/qa-guards.json` takes about 2.5 s, of which about 2.3 s is 21 subprocess calls; imports take about 0.1 s (`--help` runs in 0.5 s). cProfile: `worktree_records` runs 5 times (`git worktree list`, about 0.63 s), `pipeline_route.available` 3 times (about 1.0 s of agent probes), `task_status` 3 times (about 1.0 s). (1) Speed: within one process, compute `git worktree list` once per repo and the agent availability once per agent (memoize; never cache across processes), and drop git calls whose answer the verb already has, in `status`, `gate`, `dispatch` and `verdict`. Keep every output byte-identical. Measure before and after (`python3 -B -m cProfile -o <scratch file> scripts/factory-pipeline.py status <plan>` and the subprocess count) and put both numbers in your report. (2) Lows: (a) the dispatch spec and `tier_command` text still name `scripts/checks/english-only.py` and `scripts/checks/portable-paths.py` among the suites left to CI, although `tests/run-all.sh --within` now runs them (`WITHIN_GUARDS` in tests/run-all.sh): stop listing those as left to CI; (b) a re-QA after a QA FAIL with `--failed-suites` unions the task check suites with the failed suites: make the re-QA command `--within` only the failed suites (plus the task suites the fix delta reaches) and say so in docs/pipeline-cli.md; (c) `cleanup` still treats every `<topic>-*` branch as the plan's own, while `status` uses `Lineage.owns`: use the same ownership in cleanup; (d) the no-duplicate ERROR assertion of the `model_scope_widen` case in tests/pipeline.test.sh would not catch a re-appended '; '-joined multi-problem error: make it count the problem text. Cases in tests/pipeline.test.sh: a fake `git` on PATH that counts calls shows `status` calls `git worktree list` once per repo; the spec text no longer lists the two guard scripts as left to CI; re-QA scope; cleanup ownership. Changelog fragment changelog.d/pipeline-speed.md (### Changed, ### Fixed). CI runs on Linux: no test may depend on host tools of this Windows machine. The machine is short on memory: run one test command at a time with -j 1; stop your own test run before you report.
acceptance: status calls git worktree list once per repo and probes each agent once per process; outputs unchanged
the before and after time and subprocess count of status are in the report
the dispatch spec does not list the two guard scripts as left to CI
re-QA after a QA FAIL runs --within the failed suites
cleanup uses the same branch ownership as status

tasks.grade_reason: moves an existing guard into a script and adds it to the scoped QA guard list
tasks.objective: Backlog topic test-flakes-followups (docs/plans/backlog.md). The workspace reader guard (`reader_violations` in tests/workspace-default.test.sh, around line 148: jq readers must map paths on the same line, Python readers must use the shared helper) is inline in a long suite, so `tests/run-all.sh --within` task QA cannot run it alone and a plan once broke it with README text that only CI caught. Move the guard into a read-only check script under scripts/checks/ (same rules and output; exit non-zero on a violation; it takes the root to scan as an argument), keep the negative self-test cases in tests/workspace-default.test.sh calling the script, register the script as a run line in tests/run-all.sh and add it to `WITHIN_GUARDS` (a change that reaches it runs it under `--within`), and make tests/affected.py select it the way it selects the English-only and portable-paths guards (EXTRA). List it in scripts/README.md. Cases: tests/run-all-parallel.test.sh (a --within run of an unrelated suite also runs the reader guard, and fails on a planted raw jq reader; update the `--list-suites` expectations that list the guards), tests/affected.test.sh if the selection changes. Changelog fragment changelog.d/pipeline-speed-reader-guard.md (### Changed). Do not edit scripts/factory-pipeline.py (task verb-speed owns it). CI runs on Linux: no test may depend on host tools of this Windows machine. The machine is short on memory: run one test command at a time with -j 1; stop your own test run before you report.
acceptance: the reader guard is a check script with the same rules, and the suite's self-test calls it

tasks.grade_reason: two pattern gaps in existing guards, each with its case
tasks.objective: Backlog topic test-flakes-followups (docs/plans/backlog.md). (1) `MACHINE_PATH` in scripts/lib/plan_paths.py flags `file:` URLs that name a home directory, but not one with a host part before it (a file URL whose authority names a host, then a drive-letter or Unix home directory): flag those too, without flagging a URL whose path is not under a home directory. Cases in tests/plan-paths.test.sh. (2) The git guard's relative `git -C` check (scripts/lib/rpgf_guard/git.py, plan test-flakes) resolves a relative `-C` path against the hook cwd, but in `cd x && git -C ../y ...` the path is relative to `x`: track a preceding `cd <dir>` in the same command line (only a literal directory; anything else is 'no opinion', never a crash) and resolve against it. Cases in tests/git-guard.test.sh. Hooks stay fast (no repository scan) and never crash. Changelog fragment changelog.d/pipeline-speed-path-gaps.md (### Fixed). CI runs on Linux: no test may depend on host tools of this Windows machine. The machine is short on memory: run one test command at a time with -j 1; stop your own test run before you report.
acceptance: MACHINE_PATH flags a file: URL with a host part before a home directory
the git guard resolves git -C against a preceding literal cd in the same command
